events.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring, back) back at practice Thursday after a Wednesday DNP; DeVonta Smith still unconfirmed
events.detail: Barkley practiced Thursday after sitting Wednesday, per RotoWire, with the official participation level due on the Eagles' report. He ran 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown in Week 8. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice Wednesday and no Thursday upgrade was found. ESPN reported Barkley will not be traded before the Nov. 10 deadline. The Giants visit Philadelphia with Joe Milton starting.
events.so_what: Barkley moves back toward a start if Friday brings no setback, though a new quarterback and Elijah Mitchell taking touches cap the ceiling. Smith still needs to practice before he goes in a lineup.

source.label: RotoWire: Saquon Barkley practicing Thursday (Nov. 5)

events.headline: Christian McCaffrey back at practice Thursday; Lynch says Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel are unlikely to play Sunday
events.detail: McCaffrey (hamstring) returned to practice Thursday after sitting Wednesday, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner via RotoBaller. GM John Lynch said Evans (Achilles) and Samuel (hamstring) are unlikely to play against Las Vegas, per NFL.com. Christian Kirk was also not seen in the open portion. Kaelon Black got expanded work when McCaffrey left the Atlanta game. The official participation level and Friday's report are still to come.
events.so_what: McCaffrey is trending toward playing, but a hamstring that needed a day off is a workload risk, so keep Black rostered behind him. Plan around Evans and Samuel being out, which keeps George Kittle the steadiest target in this pass game.

source.label: RotoBaller: Christian McCaffrey back at practice on Thursday (Nov. 5)

events.headline: Bhayshul Tuten (ankle, foot) Questionable for Thursday but expected to play barring a pregame setback, per ESPN
events.detail: Tuten did not practice Tuesday through Thursday and carries a Questionable tag into Thursday night at Baltimore. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported he should play barring a setback in his pregame workout, per NFL.com, and Liam Coen has called him a game-time decision. Chris Rodriguez takes most of the work if he sits.
events.so_what: Still a forecast for a game that kicks off tonight, so start him only if he is active and you have no comparable option, because three straight DNPs point to a limited workload even if he plays. Rodriguez is the pivot if Tuten is ruled inactive.

source.label: NFL.com: NFL news roundup, Thursday Nov. 5

events.headline: Garrett Wilson (concussion) DNP for a second day Thursday; Adonai Mitchell next up vs. Kansas City
events.detail: Wilson did not practice Thursday and remains in the protocol after reporting symptoms Monday, per NFL.com. Mason Taylor (back) was upgraded to full. In Week 8 Wilson had six catches on 12 targets for 83 yards, and Mitchell had seven on nine for 142 and a touchdown, per ESPN.
events.so_what: Two missed practices in the protocol make Sunday unlikely, so plan a WR replacement now. Mitchell is the add and a start only if Wilson is ruled out. Taylor is back to a clean streaming option at tight end.

source.label: NFL.com: NFL news roundup, Thursday Nov. 5

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) upgraded to a full practice Thursday and says he is ready; Glenn says "both will play" with Braelon Allen
events.detail: Hall practiced fully Thursday after a limited Wednesday, per The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt via RotoBaller, and said he is ready to play after missing five games. Aaron Glenn has said both he and Allen will play. Allen has 504 rushing yards at 5.0 a carry across five starts. Kansas City is the Week 9 opponent.
events.so_what: Hall now looks likely to be active, but a back returning from five missed games into a stated split is a FLEX, not an RB1. Allen keeps standalone value as the back with the current role. Watch Friday for a clean report.

source.label: RotoBaller: Breece Hall logs full practice on Thursday (Nov. 5)

events.headline: Emeka Egbuka (foot) and Kenneth Gainwell (hip) upgraded to full practice Thursday ahead of Chicago
events.detail: Egbuka practiced fully Thursday after a Wednesday DNP and appears on track to return after missing two games with a concussion and the foot, per NBC Sports. Gainwell was also upgraded to full, per NFL.com. Baker Mayfield (thumb) was full as well. Friday brings the final report.
events.so_what: A full practice makes Egbuka a likely return, so he goes back into WR consideration if Friday carries no designation. Gainwell's heavy workload makes him a start.

source.label: NBC Sports: Emeka Egbuka (foot) practices in full Thursday (Nov. 5)

events.headline: A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson and Hunter Henry DNP again Thursday for New England
events.detail: All three missed a second straight practice ahead of Green Bay, per PFT: Brown (ankle, knee) has not practiced since appearing on last week's report, Henderson (illness) has missed a full week, and Henry (foot) likely needs a Friday session to avoid being ruled out. Mack Hollins (calf, IR) was limited, per NFL.com.
events.so_what: Two DNPs each makes all three unlikely, so line up replacements now rather than on Sunday morning. Rhamondre Stevenson carries the backfield volume if Henderson sits, and Eli Raridon is the tight end fill-in rather than a bid.

source.label: PFT: A.J. Brown, TreVeyon Henderson, Hunter Henry did not practice on Thursday (Nov. 5)

events.headline: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) DNP again Thursday and Malik Nabers (knee) added as a DNP for the Giants at Philadelphia
events.detail: Skattebo missed a second straight practice, with Devin Singletary next up and Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR. Nabers was listed as did not participate with a knee issue after working on the side with trainers, per CBS Sports, and told USA Today he will be good for Week 9. CBS notes the knee could relate to the ACL tear that ended his 2025 season. Friday brings designations.
events.so_what: Have a Sunday-early alternative for Skattebo, with Singletary the volume fill-in. Nabers is a wait-for-Friday rather than a bench, since he says he will play, but a knee with that history is worth a backup plan.

source.label: CBS Sports: Giants' Malik Nabers DNP due to knee injury (Nov. 5)

events.headline: Jake Ferguson (low ankle sprain) DNP again Thursday; George Pickens (hamstring) limited
events.detail: Ferguson missed a second straight practice, per NFL.com, after leaving Sunday on Dallas' first possession. Luke Schoonmaker (groin) was limited and Brevyn Spann-Ford played most of the remaining tight end snaps last week. Pickens was limited with a hamstring and KaVontae Turpin (ribs) did not practice. Dallas plays at Indianapolis.
events.so_what: Plan for a different tight end this week. Pickens being limited is worth a Friday check, though he stays a start unless he is downgraded.

source.label: NFL.com: NFL news roundup, Thursday Nov. 5

events.headline: Kyler Murray (hamstring) ruled out for Monday vs. Buffalo and week-to-week; Carson Wentz starts
events.detail: Kevin O'Connell said Thursday that Murray will not play against the Bills and is week-to-week with a hamstring strain, but IR is not being considered, per ESPN. Wentz makes the start with Max Brosmer behind him and could start beyond Monday depending on Murray's recovery.
events.so_what: Murray is a bench and the rushing premium goes with him. Wentz is a pocket passer, so the Minnesota receivers keep their volume but lose some ceiling. Wentz is a deep-league streaming option at most.

source.label: ESPN: Vikings to start QB Carson Wentz against Bills with Kyler Murray ruled out (Nov. 5)

events.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) limited Thursday for Detroit
events.detail: St. Brown was listed as limited with a rib injury on Thursday's report, per NFL.com. Jacob Saylors (neck) was also limited. Friday brings designations.
events.so_what: Limited rather than out is a good sign for a player who almost never misses, so he stays a start unless Friday adds a designation. Check before kickoff.

source.label: NFL.com: NFL news roundup, Thursday Nov. 5

events.headline: Jacoby Brissett being traded to Baltimore and expected to start Week 10; Joe Fagnano starts Thursday, Lamar Jackson is on IR and Tyler Huntley is done for the year
events.detail: Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport report the Ravens are finalizing a deal for Brissett, to be completed after Thursday's game against Jacksonville, per Pro Football Rumors. He could start Week 10 against the Chargers. Fagnano, an undrafted rookie who went 10 of 21 for 91 yards and an interception last week and practiced in an ankle brace, starts Thursday with Austin Reed backing up and Kedon Slovis as the emergency quarterback. Jackson was officially placed on IR Thursday with the thumb, sidelining him at least four games, per NFL.com, and Reed was signed to the active roster. Huntley's turf toe ends his season. ESPN's Dan Graziano suggested Baltimore, now 4-4, could take offers for Derrick Henry, who has been under 60 rushing yards for three straight games; Minnesota and Green Bay were named as possible fits, per PFR. Zay Flowers had no catches on five targets Sunday.
events.so_what: Thursday is the worst version of this offense, so sit Flowers and Mark Andrews if you have a Sunday option and lower Henry against stacked boxes. Brissett changes Week 10 onward: a working veteran passer restores Flowers as a start and gives Andrews real TD odds, though he is no streamer himself. Jackson is an IR stash only. Henry's value would swing on a landing spot, and nothing has been agreed.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: Ravens finalizing trade for Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Sam Darnold (quad, cracked rib) ruled out for Week 9; Drew Lock (elbow) expected to start vs. Arizona as Rashid Shaheed (knee) misses practice
events.detail: Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday that Darnold misses Sunday's game with a quad injury from late in Monday's loss, and that he also cracked a rib on the game's second play. "It's going to be week to week for Sam," Macdonald said; he won't go on IR. Lock is expected to start but was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough with a right elbow injury that has kept him out of the last two games. He went 19 of 26 for 235 yards and three touchdowns at Arizona in Week 2. Jalen Milroe is getting added reps and Seattle signed Adrian Martinez to the practice squad. Shaheed did not practice Wednesday, per John Boyle via RotoWire, and needs some practice work to have a chance. Left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) also remains out, per NBC Sports.
events.so_what: Lock is a matchup streamer with an arm question, not a safe one, and a thrown-through elbow is what to watch on Friday's report. Jaxon Smith-Njigba stays a start, since his target volume doesn't depend on who is throwing. Keep Shaheed on the bench until he practices. Milroe has real konami upside if the elbow goes wrong, so he is a deep stash and nothing more until he is named.

source.label: NFL.com: Seahawks QB Sam Darnold to miss Week 9 game vs. Cardinals (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Eagles to start Joe Milton in Week 9, replacing Tanner McKee after a run of losses
events.detail: NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reports Milton will make his first Eagles start Sunday against the Giants, per Pro Football Rumors. Philadelphia averaged 15 points in McKee's starts, all losses, and McKee is at 5.6 yards per attempt with a 76.6 passer rating. The offense has not topped 25 points or 350 yards in a game this year. Milton joined off Dallas' practice squad after Jalen Hurts went on season-ending IR with blood clots. This reverses Nick Sirianni's post-Week 8 statement that McKee stayed the starter.
events.so_what: Milton is a one-week experiment, not a streamer until he shows something, though his arm and legs give him more ceiling than McKee at 4 points a pass TD with the konami premium on any rushing. Eagles pass catchers get more variance rather than more value. Don't chase a bid off the name change.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: Eagles to start QB Joe Milton in Week 9 (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Brandon Aiyuk files for reinstatement and reports to the 49ers Friday; a release is considered the likeliest outcome
events.detail: Aiyuk filed to come off the reserve/left squad list, per Adam Schefter, and will report Friday, per agent Drew Rosenhaus, who said he is "healthy and ready." He has not played since tearing his ACL, MCL and meniscus in October 2024. PFR considers a release more likely than a return, at $5.09 million in cap space saved; a trade before Tuesday's deadline is possible but no team has been willing so far. San Francisco is looking for a receiver.
events.so_what: Two years off the field makes him a stash, not a start, wherever he lands. Check your wire because he may be unrostered, and treat a cheap add as a lottery ticket only if you have an idle bench spot. Real value would need a destination and a few weeks of practice.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk files for reinstatement (Nov. 4)

events.headline: David Montgomery (groin) ruled out for Week 9 and week-to-week; Woody Marks starts at the Chargers
events.detail: DeMeco Ryans ruled Montgomery out Wednesday, his third straight miss since the Week 5 injury, and called him week-to-week, per NBC Sports. Montgomery has 138 rushing yards at 2.7 a carry this year. Marks had 19 carries for 66 yards and a 15-yard catch against the Giants in Week 7, and 15 carries for 56 and two catches for 25 against Jacksonville. Houston comes off a Week 8 bye.
events.so_what: Marks is a volume RB2/FLEX with a poor per-carry rate, so his value is the workload and TD chances rather than yards. Montgomery is a bench hold, with a Week 10 return uncertain. Don't overpay to add a backup in this running game.

source.label: NBC Sports: Ryans says Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 9 (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol; Shedeur Sanders takes first-team reps and is the likely Week 9 starter at New Orleans
events.detail: Watson reported symptoms Tuesday morning, two days after a helmet-to-helmet hit in the 26-7 loss to Pittsburgh, per ESPN. Todd Monken did not rule him out but said clearing is "a little more difficult for a quarterback" without practice reps. Sanders has thrown three passes this year; he started seven games as a rookie in 2025 with 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. ESPN's fantasy desk rates Quinshon Judkins a low-end RB2 in a good matchup and Harold Fannin Jr. the most reliable Cleveland pass catcher if Sanders plays.
events.so_what: Sanders has some konami value on scrambles but his rookie turnover rate makes him a streamer only in the deepest pinch, with INTs costing just -1 the one comfort. Lower the wide receivers until the quarterback settles. Judkins holds up best here as long as Cleveland keeps the game close.

source.label: ESPN: Browns QB Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol; status vs. Saints unclear (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Jordyn Tyson limited in his first practice since a hamstring injury; Travis Etienne Jr. timeline still open and Saints claim Audric Estime
events.detail: Tyson, the Saints' first-round pick, had his practice window opened Wednesday and was limited, his first work after hamstring setbacks kept him out of the first seven games, per Yahoo and Pro Football Rumors. His Week 9 status is unclear. Etienne has been out since Sept. 27 and is eligible after the Week 8 bye; Kellen Moore said he would be evaluated before any decision on practice, per WWL's Ross Jackson via RotoWire. New Orleans also claimed Estime off waivers from Cleveland as depth behind Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson. Left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. is also in a return window after ankle surgery.
events.so_what: An opened window is not an activation. Tyson is a stash with a practice week to prove first, so plan around Week 10 or later rather than a start against Cleveland. The same goes for Etienne. Estime is not a bid unless the backs ahead of him start missing games.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: Saints LT Banks underwent ankle surgery, in IR-return window (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Jeremiyah Love on IR with a high-ankle sprain, 4-to-5 weeks; Tyler Allgeier leads and Bam Knight misses Wednesday in concussion protocol
events.detail: Arizona placed Love on injured reserve Tuesday, per Darren Urban, and Ian Rapoport reports a right high-ankle sprain with a 4-to-5 week recovery. It is his third ankle injury as a rookie. RotoWire expects Allgeier to lead the backfield starting at Seattle, after he played all 40 second-half and overtime snaps per PFF with 11 carries for 147 yards and five catches for 44 yards, and a touchdown each way. Knight did not practice Wednesday, per Theo Mackie, and NBC Sports rates him unlikely to play Sunday; Mike LaFleur said he had been planned as a top-two back before the Week 8 injuries. James Conner (foot, on IR) won't return this week. Evan Hull is the primary backup if Knight sits.
events.so_what: Love goes to an IR slot if you have one, and that timeline points to a return around Week 13 or 14, so he is a hold rather than a drop. Allgeier is a start on volume now that the job is his for a month, but the 147 yards came largely on two long runs and Seattle is next, so expect RB2/FLEX production rather than a repeat. Knight has stash value once he clears protocol, and LaFleur's comment gives it a real basis. Conner stays an IR stash.

source.label: RotoWire: Bam Knight absent from practice Wednesday (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Gardner Minshew starts for Arizona at Seattle as Jacoby Brissett heads to Baltimore; Michael Wilson (ribs) limited and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) on IR
events.detail: Mike LaFleur confirmed Monday that Minshew starts with rookie Carson Beck as the backup. Brissett, benched in Sunday's third quarter after going 10 of 23 for 119 yards and an interception, is being traded to Baltimore. Minshew went 17 of 23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns in the 33-30 overtime win at Dallas. Wilson caught 8 of a team-high 15 targets for 111 yards with broken ribs and was limited Wednesday, per RotoWire. Bourne (26 catches, 263 yards, no touchdowns) is on IR with a season-ending fractured tibia. Reggie Virgil practiced fully Wednesday after a Week 8 goalpost collision and is expected to play, per NBC Sports. Simi Fehoko played 40 of 81 snaps at Dallas with one catch for 17 yards.
events.so_what: With Brissett gone the quarterback job is Minshew's rather than a one-week look, but Seattle is next and a pocket quarterback at 4 points a pass TD has little floor, so he isn't a streamer yet. Wilson's target count makes him the receiver to start here as long as his ribs keep him limited rather than out. Bourne is a drop, and Fehoko has the snaps but not the targets behind Trey McBride and Wilson.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: NFL news live updates (Nov. 2-4)

events.headline: Christian Watson (broken rib) limited Wednesday and undecided for Week 9 at New England
events.detail: Watson was limited Wednesday, days after breaking a rib in the win over Carolina. Passing game coordinator Jason Vrable said earlier in the week he is sore but "doing great," adding "we'll see as the week goes," per The Athletic's Matt Schneidman via RotoWire. Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant would get more snaps behind Matthew Golden if he sits.
events.so_what: Limited is progress, but even if active he carries an early-exit risk, and that's a poor bet in a boom-or-bust role. Treat him as a bench piece until he practices fully. Golden is the Packers receiver who gains the most if Watson sits.

source.label: SicScore: 2026 NFL Week 9 injury report (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs "probably on the way out" of Indianapolis, per PFR; Daniel Jones also on the trade radar and Anthony Richardson the hold
events.detail: PFR's Sam Robinson says Taylor and Downs are probably leaving as the Colts sell before the Nov. 10 deadline, after trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and firing Chris Ballard. Taylor (eight carries in the 42-7 loss to Jacksonville, fewest since October 2023) has not requested a trade; Denver, Green Bay, Minnesota, the Giants and Seattle have been named in talks, and CBS' Aditi Kinkhabwala was earlier assured Indianapolis wasn't soliciting offers. Downs asked out. Jeremy Fowler reports Jones is on the trade radar, Adam Schefter says Minnesota could consider him, and a $10.51 million injury guarantee vesting in 2027 is a reason to bench him. Shane Steichen said Monday "Daniel gives us the best chance to win right now."
events.so_what: Taylor stays a start while he is a Colt with Dallas next, but a move into a shared backfield costs touches, and a trade makes Seth McGowan the stash to own. Downs is a hold pending a destination. Any Jones exit or benching opens Richardson, whose rushing scores at RB rates under the konami premium, so he is the deep stash here.

source.label: Pro Football Rumors: Colts' Daniel Jones on trade radar? (Nov. 4)

events.headline: Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet split Seattle's backfield in a 34-17 loss; Emanuel Wilson gets no carries
events.detail: Price had 10 carries for 29 yards and caught 2 of 4 targets for 8 yards. Charbonnet, in his first game since tearing his ACL in January, had 6 carries for 23 yards and caught 3 of 4 targets for 6 yards. They alternated starts on the first four drives, then Price played consecutive series and opened the second half, per Gregg Bell. Wilson, 100 yards eight days earlier against Kansas City, did not carry. George Holani took the two-minute work. Seattle's backs had 61 yards on 17 carries, with left tackle Charles Cross out. Mike Macdonald said the backs "came out OK." Wilson played seven snaps, all on special teams, per RotoWire. Charbonnet is still managing the knee.
events.so_what: Price has the small lead and Charbonnet's workload should grow, so neither is a safe start at home against Arizona in Week 9: the split is live and the blocking is short a left tackle. Wilson went from starter to no carries in one week, which makes him the drop among the three.

source.label: Gregg Bell, 93.3 KJR: Price, Charbonnet no spark in Seahawks' 34-17 loss (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. draws trade interest from several teams before the Nov. 10 deadline; Steelers linked to him and Josh Downs, with Michael Pittman Jr. no closer to returning
events.detail: Ian Rapoport reports several teams have asked about Thomas, per RotoWire, though it is unclear whether Jacksonville wants to sell. He has played behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in snap share and has topped three targets in only one of seven games. Pittsburgh has been linked to Thomas and Downs, per Pro Football Rumors. Pittman has been on IR since Week 4 and said the plantar fasciitis "morphed into something else"; he only recently resumed running and has no timetable.
events.so_what: Thomas is a free roll on a landing spot rather than a start: his current role doesn't justify a lineup slot, but a move into a thinner receiver room would change that fast. Worth a bench spot only if yours is otherwise idle, given how short benches are. Pittman is a drop candidate unless you have an open IR slot.

source.label: RotoWire: Brian Thomas appealing trade target for number of teams (Nov. 3)

events.headline: Ashton Jeanty gets two carries as Mike Washington Jr. takes 25; Kubiak says it was 'my call'
events.detail: In the Raiders' 38-33 win over the Jets, Mike Washington Jr. started, carried 25 times for 83 yards (3.3 per carry, stuffed six times per ESPN), took early-down and goal-line work, and played 63% of the snaps to Jeanty's 37%. Jeanty ran twice for 9 yards and caught three passes for 64 yards as the receiving back. Klint Kubiak said, "That's my call, and Ashton is still going to be a big part of our team," and that Jeanty's pregame comments about the Jets were not a factor. Jeanty said he was told during the week that Washington would get more work. No starter has been named for Week 9 at San Francisco.
events.so_what: A planned role change matters more than Washington's inefficient 3.3 a carry. Washington has early-down and goal-line work, which is where TD points live, so he is a live FLEX. Jeanty is a matchup start on receiving yards until Kubiak shows the carries are coming back. ESPN expects a rebound; the Kubiak quote does not promise one.

source.label: Yahoo Sports: Klint Kubiak explains Ashton Jeanty's decreased role vs. Jets (Nov. 1)
